chapter: Leaving St. Louis: Toby show, Darrell Harris and Eli Rice
title: French Canadian children touch the Black musicians
summary: Traveling Michigan in a curtained bus, the band arrived at a Mackinaw ferry where children saw Black people for the first time and touched their hands to see if it rubbed off.

bands.name: Darrell Harris and his Black Diamond Orchestra

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: No, I think he's out of, anyhow, I met him in Indiana. A nice little 10 piece band; so we were to open this in Michigan, work from Sault St. Marie and on down and on up, Mackinac Islands and all that sort of thing. And that was one place I'll never forget as long as I live. We got to a place called, I think it was Mackinaw City, I don't remember but it suddenly turned hot and we had our caps on. We had our caps on trying to get straight for the people. You know with our bad hair, we could get straight for the people.

And we had a big bus, they had the busses but we had individual curtains. Must have had a 12 piece band and the bus accommodated around, say roughly 25 or 30. So the only thing you could do is look straight ahead. So the first person to meet the bus, I think there was a little ferry somewhere down there line there, were the kids. That's French Canadian country up there, you know. And these kids came down and they looked at the bus. I could see them, trying to get myself together and they looked at the bus and as if by one signal, all the shades went up and they saw these black people in there.
Some had their caps on, you know. But, these cats split and all the day they were around us. And what they were doing, they were touching hands to see if it would rub off.
They really hadn't seen them before. You ready?
